scope: Source identity, reuse license, population and decision support for rejected ENT and infectious-diseases examination drafts. This identifies evidence for revision; it does not clear a revised artifact or certify physician review.
method: Read the actual rejected draft, source metadata, retained evidence and reviewer rejection in the local revision input.

Checked primary PubMed/PMC/publisher/society pages and Europe PMC core metadata and fullTextXML. Verified candidate article identities and actual license declarations rather than inferring permission from free availability.

Separated guideline recommendations from observational diagnostic yield and matched recommendations to the proposed population and decision point. No case, source artifact or runtime code was changed.

cases.existing_gap: The current adult cystic-neck-mass draft's next PET/CT decision has one directly supporting retained source, PMID31186166. The other retained topics include neck massage/pain, migraine, obesity, sleep apnea and free-flap mortality; these do not independently support the decisive diagnostic recommendation. Do not count them toward the two-source requirement.
cases.recommended_decision: Use an adult with a persistent lateral cervical mass, a thyroid nodule and suspicious cervical-node ultrasound features, before tissue sampling. Test ultrasound-guided FNA assessment of suspicious disease versus treating the lesion as a benign cyst on imaging alone. These sources support that thyroid-associated diagnostic decision. They do not replace the missing second source for the old nondiagnostic-FNA-to-PET/CT decision.
population_and_drafting_constraints: Describe the actual thyroid and node ultrasound features, thyroid function and sampling status. Keep the diagnosis unconfirmed at this decision point.
If the answer specifies thyroglobulin or calcitonin washout, connect the test to the suspected phenotype and the ETA recommendation; do not demand both indiscriminately.
If applying a thyroid nodule size threshold, provide the size and risk category needed for the chosen guideline. Do not confuse thyroid-nodule thresholds with suspicious-node evaluation.
Avoid a suspected lymphoma or anaplastic-thyroid-cancer scenario when making routine FNA the unqualified answer; ESR identifies core biopsy as preferred in those settings.
The final revised artifact still requires retained-quote/hash checks, independent public-payload and companion-case distinctness review, and the real review gates.

cases.existing_gap: The current answer categorically selects PET/CT for community-onset MRSA bacteremia after delayed clearance and fever, despite a drained forearm abscess and negative TEE. PMID35331165 supports occult-focus risk and potential diagnostic benefit, but explicitly cannot establish which subgroup benefits most. The mortality/antibiotic-route/combination-treatment sources do not independently support the next-imaging decision.
cases.recommended_decision: Test whether to continue a tailored assessment for occult metastatic infection in an adult with increased-risk SAB, with FDG-PET/CT as an appropriate available modality, versus declaring no further assessment necessary solely because fever resolved and echocardiography was negative. Keep the answer and rationale conditional and evidence-calibrated.
population_and_drafting_constraints: Document active therapy, follow-up culture timing/results, echocardiographic evaluation, source-control status and symptom/exam-directed evaluation. A negative TEE does not address every extracardiac focus.

Do not claim PET/CT is compulsory, proven superior to all alternative imaging, or proven to improve survival in this individual. Do not use it to replace appropriate blood cultures or echocardiography.

If relying on the 2026 IDSA whole-body-imaging consensus, make the patient match its increased-risk, unknown-focus population after appropriate initial evaluation. The current drained-forearm-abscess vignette cannot simply be labeled unknown-source without revision.
Avoid categorical duration-of-antibiotic claims based only on older complicated/uncomplicated labels; duration is outside the proposed diagnostic decision.

Retain the guideline's bacteremia indication section, not an unrelated fever-of-unknown-origin, prosthetic-valve or spinal-infection paragraph. Then verify the literal quote is present in the actual generated source passage.

sources.title: [18F]FDG-PET/CT in Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia: a systematic review.
sources.license_verification: Actual Europe PMC fullTextXML permissions/license and article identifiers verified.
sources.retention_eligibility: CC BY full text, already retained

decision_quotes.text: a diagnostic work-up strategy guided by clinical presentation alone is at high risk for missing relevant metastatic infections

sources.supports: Hospitalized adult SAB can have clinically silent metastatic foci; community acquisition, persistent cultures and fever increase concern. Five studies included 880 patients; the mortality subset was four studies and 804 patients.
sources.does_not_support: A firm PET mandate or a reliably identified subgroup with proven benefit. Evidence was low or very low certainty, with substantial bias and uncertainty.

sources.title: The role of [18F]FDG-PET/CT in gram-positive and gram-negative bacteraemia: A systematic review.
sources.date_note: Publication was in 2022; the later PubMed identifier/indexing must not be presented as a 2024 publication.
sources.license_verification: Europe PMC fullTextXML declares CC BY; the article publisher's copyright declaration links specifically to CC BY 4.0.
sources.retention_eligibility: CC BY full text; optional supporting evidence

decision_quotes.text: Both found significantly higher detection of metastatic foci in PET/CT recipients compared to controls
decision_quotes.location: Results; Identification and location of foci by PET/CT

sources.supports: Diagnostic yield in observational bacteremia cohorts, predominantly gram-positive and often SAB; two studies compared detection against controls.
sources.does_not_support: A mandatory PET recommendation, causal survival benefit or broad extrapolation to gram-negative bacteremia. It overlaps evidence in the other review.

current_guideline_context.title: IDSA/ESCMID 2026 Consensus Statements on Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia: Risk Stratification, Diagnostic Evaluation, and Management of Adults and Children
current_guideline_context.type: Society consensus statements; statement 5 addresses whole-body imaging
current_guideline_context.license: Compatible CC BY/CC0 reuse license not verified
current_guideline_context.retention_eligibility: Context only: no verified PubMed/PMC identity or compatible full-text reuse license for pinning in the present evidence pipeline
current_guideline_context.supports: For adults with increased-risk SAB and an unknown focus after initial evaluation, the panel suggests whole-body imaging such as PET/CT or combinations of imaging selected for likely sites. It presupposes follow-up cultures, echocardiography and appropriate targeted evaluation.
current_guideline_context.does_not_support: Treating PET/CT as the sole acceptable modality or claiming established mortality/relapse superiority. Do not invent a PMID or relabel website access as a reuse license.

implementation_notes: Pin the exact selected PMIDs instead of reusing broad neck* AND mass* searches. Preserve each article's real title, publication date, PMID/PMCID, source URL and license.
No broadened NC/ND exception is needed: two CC BY sources exist for the ENT pivot and a CC BY guideline plus systematic review exist for the calibrated SAB assessment decision.

Check selected excerpts after ingestion. The current parse_open_text drops paragraphs shorter than 40 characters and ranks by topic overlap: the 38-character EANM source-of-infection bullet may be omitted, while the longer metastatic-infections bullet can supply direct support if retained with its bacteremia heading.

Existing OpenAI review or publication metadata does not replace artifact validation. Any revised entry requires its own exact whole-document hash, retained-source and literal-quote verification, clinical reviews, blind solution checks and independent artifact audit before release.
